question.leadin: This country was created after the United Nations passed a plan to partition Palestine at the end of 1947.
question.text: Name this Jewish state that within 24 hours of its creation was invaded by Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, and Syria.
question.clue: This nation's city of Beersheba is known as the "capital of the Negev".

swap.leadin: Under the grip of its fifth president, this country was in turmoil beginning in 1980 and culminating in 2003 when it was invaded by a "coalition of the willing."
swap.text: Name this Middle Eastern country established by the British in 1921. The first ruler of this country was the Hashemite king Faisal I.
swap.answerHtml: Iraq (or Republic of Iraq or Jumhuriyat al- Iraq )
swap.clue: Soldiers from this country were bombed on the "Highway of Death" in Operation Desert Storm during the First Gulf War.

question.text: After France was granted control of the Levant in the end of World War I, the Hashemites established an Arab Kingdom in this country and unsuccessfully fought the French. Today, this country is controversially led by Bashar al-Assad.
question.clue: This province was the main power base of a general who was defeated at the Battle of Carrhae, Marcus Licinius Crassus.

swap.text: A second oil shock occurred in 1979, partially due to this country's regime change and a subsequent war with Iraq. Shah Mohammed Reza Pahlavi was deposed as leader of this country by the Ayatollah Khomeini.
swap.clue: The newspaper Al-Shiraa is best known for exposing covert US arms sales to this country.

question.leadin: This empire was defeated at the Battle of Tours.
question.text: Name this empire founded by Muawiyah which defeated its predecessor at the Battle of Siffin. An offshoot of this empire after its fall would later form the Emirate of Cordoba under Abd al-Rahman I.
question.clue: This empire rose to power after their victory in a conflict sparked by the killing of Uthman ibn Affan.

swap.text: This Middle Eastern country is also embroiled in civil war, with former President Abdrabbuh Mansur Hadi and his Saudi allies clashing with former President Ali Abdullah Saleh and his Iran-backed Houthi allies.
swap.clue: During ancient times, it was governed from the capital of Ma'rib by an empire that fought several civil wars with the Hadramaut kingdom in this nation.

question.leadin: This treaty was partially overturned in the Treaty of Lausanne.
question.text: Name this agreement that split the Middle East between the British and the French. This agreement's conditions simultaneously violated both the earlier Balfour Declaration and the McMahon-Hussein "mick-MEH-han hoo-SAYN") Correspondence.
question.clue: It was supplemented by the Agreement of Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne and it was modified at the Conference of San Remo.

swap.leadin: The city of Konya [CONE-yah] has it all: mosques, museums, and great-power struggles for supremacy.
swap.text: The Sultanate of Rum, established by these people, was based at Konya. This Turkic dynasty won the Battles of Dandanaqan and Manzikert.
swap.clue: This group captured the Aklat Fort, and thus Romanus IV, during their greatest military victory.

question.leadin: Answer the following about medieval mapmaking.
question.text: This city's Balkhi school of geography produced many maps in the T and O style. An apocryphal account describes how a river in this city ran black with ink from the maps and books destroyed during a Mongol siege.
question.clue: This city fell to the Seljuk Turks under Tughril Beg, who thereafter ruled the city as Sultans.

swap.leadin: This successor of al-Mahdi was advised by his Barmakid vizier Yahya, and with his son al-Ma'mun established the Hosue of Wisdom.
swap.text: Identify this Islamic ruler, the subject of much of the Meadows of Gold, who presided over a high point of culture and civilization during the eighth century.
swap.answerHtml: Harun al-Rashid [or the Upright; or the Just; or the Rightly Guided; accept Aaron]
swap.clue: He even laid the groundwork for civil war by dividing the succession between his sons al-Amin and al-Ma'mun.

question.leadin: Marwan II was defeated at the Battle of the Great Zab in a revolution named for this black-bannered dynasty.
question.text: Name this dynasty which claimed legitimacy due to their descent from one of Muhammad's uncles. Caliphs Al-Mansur and Harun al-Rashid were members of this dynasty which succeeded the Umayyads.
question.clue: This dynasty defeated a general of Korean descent, Go Seonji in one battle.

swap.leadin: Founded after a Khorasan-based revolt against the Umayyads in 750 CE, this second caliphate ruled until the Mongol conquests of 1258.
swap.text: Name this dynasty founded by Abu as-Saffah, "the blood-shedder."
swap.answerHtml: ‘Abbasid Dynasty [or ‘Abbasid Caliphate or ‘Abbasids etc.; prompt on Caliphate]
swap.clue: Nominally beginning with the Battle of the Great Gab River, after which its namesake took the epithet "blood-shedder," as-Saffah, its decline began with the revolt of Babak, which compelled the import of mercenaries by al-Mu'tasim, son of Harun ar-Rashid.

question.leadin: Following the successful Battle of Yamana, this caliph oversaw the compilation of the Qur'an into a single manuscript.
question.text: Name this caliph whose ascension caused a schism between his supporters and those who supported a man reputedly addressed as "mawla" at Ghadir Khumm.
question.answerHtml: Abu Bakr [or Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq ‘Abdallāh bin Abī Quḥāfah]
question.clue: Lubaina, Zinnira, and Bilal were among the many slaves this man used his wealth to emancipate , and the rest of his money went to fund an expedition at Tabuk.

swap.text: The war between supporters of Ali and Mu'awiya was the first Muslim civil war known by this Arabic-language name. The second war known by this name would occur after Mu'awiya's death.

question.leadin: Answer some bonuses about the ridiculous misadventures of Mohammad 'Abdullah Nasr, affectionately known in Egypt as "Shaykh Mizo," [MEE-zoo] which roughly translates to "Dr. Talks-Out-His-Ass."
question.text: Less humorously, that claim got Mizo arrested in Sisi's accelerating enforcement of blasphemy laws, another victim of which called al-Bukhari, who compiled several of these stories about Muhammad, a "garbage collector."
question.answerHtml: Ḥadīth [also accept Ṣaḥīḥ in context; the technically correct plural of “Ḥadīth” is ’aḥādīth but obviously accept Ḥadīths] (the “other victim” is the telesecularist TV host Islām al-Buḥayrī, whom Sisi pardoned)

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about critical points in relations between Turkey and Greece.
swap.text: In 1999, relations worsened when the Greek military attempted to give refuge to Abdullah Ocalan, founder of this nationalist organization that aims to form a separate state for its traditionally persecuted ethnic group.
swap.answerHtml: PKK [or Kurdistan Workers’ Party; or Parti Karkerani Kurdistan; or KGK]

question.leadin: Naguib Mahfouz explored the assassination of this Egyptian president in The Day the Leader Was Killed.
question.text: Name this successor to Nasser, who pulled back from Nasserist economic policy with the Infitah program, launched the Yom Kippur War against Israel, and re-legalized political parties.
question.answerHtml: Anwar el-Sadat [do not rule people wrong for not saying “el”]
question.clue: This leader who oversaw Egypt's shift in the Cold War away from the USSR. He signed the Camp David Accords.

swap.leadin: Irish Defense Minister James Tully and a Cuban ambassador were wounded in this event, during which a crowd of people threw chairs around the victim to shield him from a hailstorm of bullets.
swap.text: Name this October 1981 event carried out by Khalid Islambouli on behalf of the Islamic Jihad at a victory parade celebrating the eighth anniversary of Operation Badr.
swap.answerHtml: Anwar Sadat assassination [or killing of Anwar Sadat; or synonyms]
swap.clue: This event took place during a commemoration of Operation Badr, during which the central figure of this event had earned the nickname "Hero of the Crossing."

question.leadin: Answer the following about King Faisal I of Iraq.
question.text: Faisal was one of the leaders attacked by this camel-riding militia, which takes its name from the Arabic for "brotherhood." This religious force helped to install Ibn Saud as ruler of Saudi Arabia, and he used them as his elite army, until they led a namesake revolt against him that was quashed at Sabilla in 1929.
question.clue: Throughout the 1920s, these people rode camels and wielded outdated guns while attacking British positions in Transjordan and Kuwait.

swap.leadin: This sultan established a still-extant cat garden in Cairo as a waqf due to his love of the animals and their special place in Islam.
swap.text: Name this ethnic Kipchak who took power after his rival Qutuz's death. This Mamluk sultan founded the Bahri Dynasty.
swap.answerHtml: Baybars I [or al-Malik al-Ẓāhir Rukn al-Dīn Baybars al-Bunduqdārī or Abu al-Futūḥ]
